name: Noel Holmes
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember an usher who set his chair beside mine.” On Saturday, near the blocks below Foundry Lofts, Noel checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I sat beside her because my own witness statement had cost me a friend. This time she chose when to sign.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a black overshirt with pearl buttons and a watch on a cracked leather band. Noel has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw, with a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. Noel leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations during a conversation.
personality: Noel carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To help a hesitant witness leave with a signed copy.
family: Katherine Lowe is Noel’s younger cousin. Noel asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Katherine remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *A red mitten*, Katherine says, “I found the other mitten in the lift. I've put the pair on a cord long enough to cover two chairs.”
connections: Elise Kapoor. A drawing of the room gives the hesitant witness a less public way to begin.

reactions.situation: The counter is busy and another visitor starts to hurry the signing
reactions.response: Noel puts a time on when the counter will be free again and protects the witness's time to read.

reactions.situation: A colleague says somebody used the wrong name in public
reactions.response: Noel offers to help correct the printed name and leaves it to the colleague whether any public explanation is wanted.

reactions.response: Noel offers to accompany them while they tell the truth.
